eligibility.evidence: E1/E2 fail (Sec 3-4): four vision-language models (OFA, Unified-IO, LLaVA, InstructBLIP) answer questions about images of classic visual illusions (Muller-Lyer, Ebbinghaus); perception is not an E2 domain and the task is image-administered, not language-administered. Human answers are authors' annotations, not data (Limitations). Borderline: LLaVA/InstructBLIP use Vicuna; illusions are named classic paradigms.

A.title: Grounding Visual Illusions in Language: Do Vision-Language Models Perceive Illusions Like Humans?

G.notes: Eligibility turns on whether image-administered perceptual illusions with Vicuna-based VLMs count under E1 and E2; I coded NO. Referee would note that 'human' answers are the authors' own expectations, never measured (Limitations), and 12 VLM checkpoints on 1,600 instances.
